name: iron street lamp post seen from above-front: round stone base with visible top, lantern with a pyramid cap seen from above
label: sky-island/si-lamppost

answer.evidence: The lantern, eaves, and post are drawn in pure front elevation with straight horizontal 1px lines at rows 6 and 12 and no visible top surface on the lantern body or cap. While the base plinth shows a top surface, base plinths do not count for the main body.

The lantern and its cap are drawn in flat front elevation with horizontal lines across rows 2 and 6 and flat rectangular panes; only the base plinth shows foreshortening, but the main body lacks any top surface.

The lantern cap and lantern housing are drawn in pure front elevation with a flat trapezoidal cap and flat rectangular window panes; rows 1-2 form only a 2px highlight/rim band rather than a foreshortened top surface. The only foreshortened surface is the base plinth, which cannot substitute for a top surface on the main body/top end.

The lantern cap, frame, and post are drawn in pure front elevation with straight horizontal edges and rectangular panes. Only the bottom plinth shows a top surface, which per the instructions cannot be credited for the main body.
